title: ReviewPlane MCP interface, version 1
description: Single source for the agent-facing contract of docs/MCP_SPEC.md: the Stage 0 tool arguments and results, the common response envelope of section 5, the trust labels of section 6, the resource URI forms of section 8, the stable error codes of section 12 and the tool availability set of section 14. x-protocol.messages is keyed by tool name, so the generated MESSAGE_TYPE_VALUES is the negotiated Stage 0 tool set and PAYLOAD_MAX_BYTES is the per-tool response bound section 13 requires. TypeScript models and validators are generated from this file; a hand-maintained equivalent in apps/mcp-server is a review failure.

channels.review: Named review retrieval and review lifecycle (section 7.6).
channels.command: Tool arguments sent by an agent client.
channels.refusal: The section 5 error envelope and its stable section 12 code.

project_current.description: The project, workspace and policy summary the agent session is bound to (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.1). It is how an agent validates that a named review belongs to the project it is working in before acting on it.

agent_session_status.description: Agent-session identity, negotiated capabilities and associated browser sessions (section 7.1). The browser sessions carry the control epoch a capture must present.

review_get.description: One review resolved by immutable identifier or project-scoped slug, with a bounded page of findings and resource links rather than embedded images (sections 7.6 and 13).

review_claim.description: The review after the current agent session claimed it (section 7.6).

review_update_status.description: The review after an agent-permitted status change. An agent may not set a review to ACCEPTED; the status enumeration this tool accepts does not contain it.

finding_get.description: One finding, its annotations, its evidence links and its latest verification (section 7.7).

finding_claim.description: The finding after the current agent session claimed it with optimistic concurrency (section 7.7).

finding_update_status.description: The finding after an agent-permitted transition of section 7.7. The terminal state available to an agent is AWAITING_HUMAN_REVIEW.

finding_add_comment.description: The comment as recorded, attributed to the agent session (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 18).

finding_submit_verification.description: The verification record a submission created (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 19). It is a claim with evidence and never a resolution: its status is submitted and only a human may accept it.

browser_take_screenshot.description: A verified screenshot artefact, returned as a resource link and never as inline image bytes (sections 7.4 and 13). The capture is page-derived, so the response is labelled untrusted_browser_content.

session_initialisation_request.description: Session initialisation input of docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 4: client identity, project and workspace hints, and client capabilities.

session_initialisation_result.description: Session initialisation output of section 4. Ambiguous project association is refused with PROJECT_CONTEXT_AMBIGUOUS and candidates rather than resolved by guessing, so this shape is never produced for an ambiguous binding.

review_get_input.description: Arguments of review_get. review accepts an immutable identifier or a project-scoped slug such as bugs-on-homepage, resolved inside the current project only.

finding_update_status_input.description: Arguments of finding_update_status. The status enumeration is the agent-permitted set of section 7.7 and structurally excludes every final disposition.

finding_submit_verification_input.description: Arguments of finding_submit_verification, in the shape of section 7.7.

browser_take_screenshot_input.description: Arguments of browser_take_screenshot. Stage 0 accepts the verification purpose only.

tool_refusal.description: The section 5 error envelope. It is not a frame: a refusal carries no type-selected data, so it is validated on its own rather than through the payload dispatch.

frame_too_large.description: The encoded response exceeded its byte bound. Detected on the raw bytes before deserialisation.

malformed_json.description: The response was not well-formed JSON, or was truncated.

unsupported_protocol_version.description: protocol_version was absent, not an integer, or not a version this build accepts (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 14).

unknown_message_type.description: type was absent or not a Stage 0 tool. An unknown tool is rejected rather than dispatched to a default.

payload_too_large.description: The data object exceeded the byte bound declared for its tool, which is the per-tool size limit of docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 13.

schema_violation.description: The response parsed but did not satisfy the schema for its tool.

untrusted_content_mislabelled.description: The response carried page-derived or uploaded content while declaring a trusted label. ADR-0010 and docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 6 forbid returning page content without an untrusted label, and the rule lives in the codec rather than in JSON Schema because the envelope's label has to be conditioned on what the type-selected data turned out to contain.

resource_uri_forms.description: The resource URI forms of docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 8 that Stage 0 serves. A resource enforces exactly the authorisation its equivalent tool does, so a URI belonging to another project is unreachable rather than merely undocumented. trace:// is listed in section 8 and is deliberately absent from Stage 0, which persists no traces.

stage_0_tool_availability.description: The tool availability set docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 14 requires a client to be able to rely on. It equals x-protocol.messages, so a tool cannot be advertised without a result schema. Everything else in the section 7 catalogue is unavailable in Stage 0 and is absent from tools/list rather than present and failing: no inbox tools, no development-service tools, no visual inspection, no completion gates, no secret tools and no review listing or search.

agent_transitions.description: The finding transitions docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.7 permits an agent, written as from:to. The agent-facing status enumeration cannot express a final disposition at all, which is why the denial of AGENTS.md is structural here and a runtime check only in the domain layer beneath it.

identifier.description: Opaque durable identifier (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 3). Consumers MUST treat the value as opaque: the schema bounds only its length and character class and never its documented prefix.

request_id.description: Identifier of the tool call, echoed in every envelope so a refusal in a transcript can be joined to the audit record it produced (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 5).

idempotency_key.description: Caller-chosen key for a state-changing tool (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 10). It is scoped to actor, tool and project: reuse with the same arguments returns the first result and creates no second record, and reuse with different arguments is refused with IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC, with a mandatory trailing Z.

slug.description: Project-scoped human alias, for example bugs-on-homepage. It is unique among active reviews of one project and not across projects, so the same slug in another project MUST resolve as not found rather than as somebody else's review (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.6).

review_selector.description: How an agent names a review: an immutable identifier or a project-scoped slug. Both resolve inside the current project only, and no cross-project search is performed.

project_hint.description: Project the client believes it is working in, by slug or identifier. It narrows the credential's binding and never widens it: a hint naming a project the credential is not bound to is refused.

workspace_hint.description: Filesystem root of the checkout the agent is working in, used to pick a workspace when the project has more than one.

client_name.description: Agent client name as it identifies itself, for example claude-code. It is descriptive and never an authorisation input.

client_version.description: Agent client version as reported. unknown is accepted, because several clients do not report one.

title_text.description: Human-authored title. Rendered as text and never as markup, and never followed as an instruction when it reached the record from a page.

body_text.description: Human-authored or agent-authored prose: a description, instruction, comment, resolution note or verification summary.

reason_text.description: Short operator-facing explanation. Never carries credentials (docs/SECURITY.md section 18).

captured_url.description: Absolute URL a finding or capture was taken at. It is page-derived and therefore untrusted (ADR-0010): bounded in length and character class, displayed as text, never executed and never followed as an instruction.

resource_uri.description: One of the docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 8 resource URI forms. A resource enforces the same authorisation as the tool that returned the link.

content_path.description: Path that serves artefact bytes for a short-lived, subject-bound grant (ADR-0019). It is not a credential: the caller must still authenticate as the grant's subject, which is why the identifier may appear in a URL at all.

branch_name.description: Version-control branch. Recorded on a verification so a human can see which branch the claim was made from.

commit_sha.description: Version-control commit. A verification commit MUST differ from the commit the finding was captured at: a fix cannot exist at the revision the defect was recorded from.

sha256_hex.description: Lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest, as verified by the control plane from the stored bytes.

media_type.description: Media type of stored artefact bytes. Bounded to the types Stage 0 stores; active markup is not among them (docs/SECURITY.md section 13).

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor (docs/API.md section 6). Its contents are an implementation detail and MUST NOT be parsed by a client.

page_limit.description: Maximum records in one page. Bounded here rather than by the caller's optimism, because an unbounded response is the failure mode docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 13 exists to prevent.

record_count.description: A count of records, bounded so a count cannot itself be unbounded.

version_number.description: Optimistic-concurrency version. A caller presenting a stale value is refused with VERSION_CONFLICT and the current version in the details (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 11).

control_epoch.description: Monotonic browser-control epoch (ADR-0007). A command presenting a superseded epoch is refused with CONTROL_EPOCH_STALE rather than executed against a browser somebody else now controls.

byte_size.description: Byte length the control plane verified.

pixel_extent.description: A dimension in device pixels of a stored image.

css_pixel_offset.description: An offset in CSS pixels within the captured document.

device_scale_factor.description: Device pixel ratio of the capture.

marker_number.description: Ordinal shown inside a numbered marker, so the annotation list and the overlay name the same mark.

normalised_coordinate.description: A coordinate normalised to the artefact content rectangle, inclusive of both bounds (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 16).

retry_after_ms.description: How long to wait before retrying, returned with RATE_LIMITED.

expires_in_seconds.description: Remaining life of a short-lived grant or credential.

trust_label.description: Provenance of the content in a response (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 6). Page-derived content MUST NOT be returned without an untrusted label, and mixed marks a response that carries both control-plane facts and page-derived or uploaded content, with the untrusted members named in untrusted_fields.

instruction_policy.description: The single-valued policy of docs/SECURITY.md section 11. It rides on every response rather than only on untrusted ones, so an agent never has to infer the absence of a rule from the absence of a field.

untrusted_field_path.description: Dotted path of a member of data that is page-derived or uploaded. It exists so mixed is actionable: an agent can tell which members of an otherwise trusted record came from a page.

warning_code.description: Why a response is less than a client asked for while still being a success. A degradation is a warning and not a failure (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 8.3): a client that cannot consume image content still completes the workflow.

error_class.description: Stable refusal code (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 12). Adding a code is additive within a protocol version and a client MUST tolerate a code it does not recognise. This enumeration MUST equal x-protocol.error_classes.

message_type.description: A Stage 0 tool. This enumeration is the tool availability set of docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 14 and MUST equal the keys of x-protocol.messages, so a tool the server advertises always has a result schema and a bound.

agent_capability.description: A capability an agent credential may carry (docs/SECURITY.md section 6.3). A tool requires one, and a credential without it is refused with AUTHORISATION_DENIED. An agent session cannot grant itself a capability beyond its issued set (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 11).

agent_review_status.description: Review statuses an agent may request. ACCEPTED is absent by construction, which is the AGENTS.md authority rule expressed as a type rather than as a runtime check. The docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.6 list also named blocked; docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 14 has no such review status and takes precedence, so a blocked agent records the block on the finding it is stuck on.

agent_finding_status.description: Finding statuses an agent may request, taken from the transition list of docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.7. RESOLVED, WONT_FIX and DUPLICATE are absent: an agent that cannot name a final disposition cannot request one, so the refusal does not depend on a check anybody could forget.

finding_source.description: Whether a human or an agent authored the finding. The acceptance authority rule is decided on it for the life of the finding.

artefact_kind.description: Artefact kind (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 20). Stage 0 evidence is a screenshot.

verification_status.description: Status of a verification submission (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 19). An agent produces submitted and nothing else; accepted and rejected are human decisions.

actor_type.description: Who acted (docs/EVENTS.md section 5). The distinction between human_user and agent_session is what the acceptance authority rules are decided on.

screenshot_purpose.description: Why a capture is being taken. Stage 0 accepts verification only: a capture is evidence, and an unclassified capture cannot be filed under a retention class.

review_include.description: Optional sections of a review response. staleness is deliberately absent: staleness calculation is Stage 2, and a field that would have to be guessed is omitted rather than falsely reported (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 24).

finding_include.description: Optional sections of a finding response.

session_include.description: Optional sections of an agent-session status response.

actor_reference.description: An acting principal. The type is always present, because an authority rule that depends on it must never fall back to a default.

id.description: Identifier of the acting principal, where one exists.

display.description: Human-readable label. Never used to establish identity.

viewport.description: Browser viewport in CSS pixels plus the device pixel ratio. A finding records the viewport it was seen at so it can be reproduced at that size.

device_scale_factor.description: Device pixel ratio the capture was taken at.

scroll_position.description: Document scroll offset in CSS pixels at capture time.

content_rectangle.description: Intrinsic pixel extent of a stored image, which is the frame annotation geometry is normalised against (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 16).

annotation_geometry.description: Normalised geometry against the artefact content rectangle. Which members a type uses is fixed by the review protocol's own vocabulary; every member here lies between 0 and 1 inclusive.

x.description: Left edge for a box, position for a point or marker, tail for an arrow.

y.description: Top edge for a box, position for a point or marker, tail for an arrow.

width.description: Box width, for a rectangle or an ellipse.

height.description: Box height, for a rectangle or an ellipse.

project_reference.description: A project the agent credential is bound to. It is the shape returned in PROJECT_CONTEXT_AMBIGUOUS details, so an agent can disambiguate rather than be told only that it failed.

slug.description: Project slug, which is what a project_hint is usually written as.

workspace_reference.description: The checkout the agent is working in (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 9). Stage 0 has no connector, so a workspace is registered administratively and is absent when none is registered; a verification submitted without one is accepted with a warning rather than refused, because the branch cannot be corroborated but the evidence still can.

root_path.description: Filesystem root of the checkout, which is what workspace_hint matches on.

dirty.description: Whether the checkout has uncommitted changes.

policy_summary.description: What the project requires of an agent before work counts as done, and what it will never let an agent do. The negative statements are as load-bearing as the positive ones: an agent that reads agent_may_accept_findings: false learns the boundary of docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 15 rather than discovering it as a refusal.

agent_may_accept_findings.description: Always false. A human-authored finding is accepted by a human; an agent submits verification and marks the finding AWAITING_HUMAN_REVIEW.

verification_required.description: Whether a completion claim must carry verification evidence. Always true in Stage 0: AGENTS.md forbids claiming a fix without it.

secret_tools_available.description: Always false in Stage 0. No secret tool is exposed at all, which is the strongest form of the no-disclosure rule of docs/SECURITY.md section 12.1.

required_viewports.description: Viewports UI-facing work must be checked at (AGENTS.md "Browser-facing work").

server_capabilities.description: What this server can do for this session (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 4 and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 8.3). A false value is a fact the client can plan around, which is what makes degradation clear rather than surprising.

browser_live.description: Whether a human can watch the browser session live.

image_resources.description: Whether this session will be served image content. It is the negotiated result of the client's own image capability, not a property of the server alone.

human_takeover.description: Whether a human may take browser control from the agent.

review_inbox.description: Whether inbox tools are available. False in Stage 0: the inbox workflow of section 9 is Stage 1, and the tools are absent rather than present and empty.

managed_messages.description: Whether the server pushes messages to the client. False: agents retrieve explicitly (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 8.3).

session_resume.description: Whether an interrupted session can be resumed.

client_capabilities.description: What the client says it can consume (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 4). image_content false is the case docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 8.3 requires clear degradation for: the workflow still completes, with resource links, text and a warning instead of image content.

resources.description: Whether the client can read MCP resources.

image_content.description: Whether the client can consume image content.

managed_messages.description: Whether the client can receive pushed messages.

session_resume.description: Whether the client can resume a session.

warning.description: A degradation or a truncation that did not stop the call succeeding.

detail.description: What the client can do about it, where there is something to do.

error_details.description: Machine-readable detail for a refusal. Bounded rather than free-form, so a refusal cannot become a channel for arbitrary content.

current_version.description: Version the record actually holds, returned with VERSION_CONFLICT.

current_epoch.description: Epoch the browser session actually holds, returned with CONTROL_EPOCH_STALE.

field.description: Path of the offending argument, where one is at fault.

candidates.description: Projects the credential is bound to, returned with PROJECT_CONTEXT_AMBIGUOUS. The server never picks one: it returns the list so the agent can name the project it means.

items.description: A project the agent may name in project_hint.

required_evidence.description: Evidence a completion claim must carry, returned with EVIDENCE_REQUIRED.

items.description: Name of a missing piece of evidence.

allowed_transitions.description: Transitions the agent may perform from the finding's current status, returned when a transition is refused. The refusal states what is possible rather than only what is not.

retry_after_ms.description: How long to wait before retrying, returned with RATE_LIMITED.

tool_error.description: The refusal object of docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 5. The code is the stable vocabulary of section 12; the message is for a human and is never parsed.

retryable.description: Whether retrying the same call unchanged could succeed. It is explicit so a client does not have to infer retryability from the code.

artefact_link.description: A reference to evidence, never the evidence itself (docs/MCP_SPEC.md sections 7.6 and 13). content_path serves the bytes for a short-lived grant bound to this agent session (ADR-0019); an agent that wants the image fetches it with its own credential or reads the resource, and neither the tool result nor the review response ever embeds it.

role.description: What the artefact shows in context, such as before or after.

resource_uri.description: MCP resource URI for the artefact.

content_path.description: Path serving the bytes for the grant minted with this response.

content_type.description: Media type of the stored bytes.

sha256.description: Digest the control plane verified from the stored bytes. It is what ties a claim in a transcript to bytes on disk.

size_bytes.description: Byte length the control plane verified.

content_rectangle.description: Intrinsic pixel extent of an image artefact.

trust.description: Provenance of the bytes. A capture or an upload is untrusted.

instruction_policy.description: The policy that applies to anything legible inside the artefact.

annotation_view.description: One mark on a finding's original screenshot, as an agent sees it (ADR-0006). The geometry is normalised and the original is untouched.

artefact_id.description: Original artefact the geometry is normalised against.

label.description: Text alternative for the mark, which is what makes the annotation legible to an agent that never renders the image.

marker_number.description: Ordinal shown inside a numbered marker.

comment_view.description: One comment on a finding (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 18). Comments are append-only and the author type is always explicit.

author.description: Who wrote it. An agent comment is clearly attributed to the agent session.

verification_checks.description: The checks a verification claims to have performed (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 19). They are recorded as claims by the agent and are never treated as proof on their own: the artefacts are the evidence.

reproduced_before.description: Whether the agent reproduced the defect before changing anything.

console_errors_reviewed.description: Whether console output was reviewed after the change.

network_failures_reviewed.description: Whether failed network requests were reviewed after the change.

accessibility_checked.description: Whether keyboard navigation and visible focus were checked.

verification_view.description: A submitted claim with evidence (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 19). Its status is submitted: a verification is not a resolution, and the human decision that follows is not available to an agent at all.

summary.description: What was changed and how it was checked.

branch.description: Branch the fix was made on.

commit.description: Commit the fix was made in.

tested_viewports.description: Viewports the fix was checked at.

checks.description: Checks the agent claims to have performed.

artefacts.description: Evidence the submission rests on, as links rather than bytes.

review_view.description: A review as an agent sees it. The captured branch and commit are on the record because the point of a review is to still mean something after the code has moved on.

slug.description: Project-scoped alias, which is the name a human gave the agent.

description.description: Instruction from the human who created the review.

version.description: Version to present on the next write.

captured_branch.description: Branch the findings were captured from.

captured_commit.description: Commit the findings were captured from.

captured_workspace_id.description: Workspace the captured application was running in.

source_browser_session_id.description: Browser session the review was captured from. The review outlives it.

claimed_by.description: Agent session currently working the review.

finding_count.description: Findings in the review, which is not the number returned in one page.

updated_at.description: Time of the last accepted mutation.

finding_view.description: A finding as an agent sees it, with the captured context that makes it reproducible after the browser session has gone. untrusted_fields names the members that came from a page, which is what makes the mixed trust label of the enclosing response actionable.

title.description: Short statement of what is wrong.

description.description: Detail the agent needs to reproduce and judge the finding.

source.description: Whether a human or an agent authored it. A human-authored finding can only be finally accepted by a human.

version.description: Version to present on the next write.

url.description: URL the finding was captured at. Page-derived and untrusted.

viewport.description: Viewport and device pixel ratio at capture time.

scroll_position.description: Document scroll offset at capture time.

captured_commit.description: Commit the capture was taken from.

screenshot_artefact_id.description: Original screenshot the annotations are placed on.

acceptance_criteria.description: What a resolution has to demonstrate.

untrusted_fields.description: Members of this record that are page-derived. An empty list is impossible: url is always page-derived, so the array is required and always populated.

items.description: Dotted path of a page-derived member.

browser_session_view.description: A browser session the agent session may capture from, with the control epoch a capture must present. The epoch is here so an agent does not have to guess it, and a superseded one is refused rather than executed (ADR-0007).

viewport.description: Viewport the session is running at.

service_origin.description: Origin of the published development service the session is bound to.

session_initialisation_request.description: Session initialisation input of docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 4. The client name and version come from the MCP initialize handshake; the hints and capabilities come from the endpoint the client was configured with, because MCP's own handshake has nowhere to carry them.

project_hint.description: Project the client believes it is working in.

workspace_hint.description: Checkout root the client is working in.

client_identity.description: The connecting client, as it names itself. It is recorded on the agent session for the audit trail and is never an authorisation input: the credential decides what the session may do.

session_initialisation_result.description: Session initialisation output of docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 4.

agent_session_id.description: The agent session this connection acts as.

project.description: Project resolved from the credential and the hints.

workspace.description: Workspace resolved, where the project has one.

capabilities.description: What the server will do for this session.

granted_capabilities.description: Capabilities the credential carries. The session cannot exceed them.

expires_at.description: When the credential expires. A call after it is refused with AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED rather than partly executed.

refresh_source_state.description: Re-read the workspace branch and commit before answering, for the recheck docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.1 recommends before verification.

review_get_input.description: Arguments of review_get. The review is resolved inside the current project only: a slug that exists in another project is not found, and no cross-project search happens (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.6).

review.description: Immutable identifier or project-scoped slug, for example bugs-on-homepage.

findings_limit.description: Maximum findings in this page. Defaults to 20 and is capped at the schema maximum.

status.description: Requested status. ACCEPTED is not expressible.

expected_version.description: Version the agent last read. A concurrent claim is refused with VERSION_CONFLICT and the current metadata.

finding_update_status_input.description: Arguments of finding_update_status. status is the agent-permitted enumeration, so no argument exists that would ask for a final disposition of a human's finding.

status.description: Requested status, from the section 7.7 list.

resolution_note.description: What was changed and how it was checked. Required to reach FIXED_UNVERIFIED: a completion claim without evidence is refused with EVIDENCE_REQUIRED.

reason.description: Why, recorded on the transition. Required to reach BLOCKED.

x-requires.detail: A blocked finding must say what is blocking it, because a human has to act on it.

body.description: Comment text. It is stored and rendered as text.

idempotency_key.description: Key for this comment, so a retried call does not produce two.

finding_submit_verification_input.description: Arguments of finding_submit_verification, in the shape of docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.7. The server validates evidence ownership and commit context: an artefact belonging to another project is refused, and a commit equal to the one the finding was captured at is not a fix.

expected_version.description: Version the agent last read, where the agent wants the submission refused if the finding moved.

summary.description: What was changed and how it was checked.

branch.description: Branch the fix was made on. It is checked against the workspace branch where a workspace is known.

commit.description: Commit the fix was made in.

tested_viewports.description: Viewports the fix was checked at.

artefact_ids.description: Evidence. At least one must be a verified screenshot in this project, captured in this project's browser-session lineage.

idempotency_key.description: Key for this submission. A duplicate produces one verification record.

browser_take_screenshot_input.description: Arguments of browser_take_screenshot. control_epoch is required by docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.4 for every browser tool, and a superseded epoch is refused with CONTROL_EPOCH_STALE rather than captured from a browser somebody else now controls.

control_epoch.description: Epoch the agent believes is current.

full_page.description: Capture the whole document rather than the viewport.

purpose.description: Why the capture is being taken. Stage 0 accepts verification only.

idempotency_key.description: Key for this capture, so a retried call does not store two artefacts.

project.description: The project this session is bound to.

workspace.description: The workspace, where one is registered.

policy.description: What the project requires and what it forbids.

project.description: Project the session is bound to.

browser_sessions.description: Browser sessions this agent session may capture from.

review_get_result.description: Payload of review_get. findings is one bounded page; findings_next_cursor is present only when more remain.

findings.description: One page of findings, oldest first, so an agent works them in the order a human recorded them.

findings_next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, present only when more findings remain.

artefact_links.description: Evidence links for the findings in this page, as links rather than bytes.

review_mutation_result.description: Payload of review_claim and review_update_status: the review as it now stands.

previous_status.description: Status before the change, absent when nothing moved.

annotations.description: Marks on the original screenshot, with their text alternatives.

comments.description: Comments on the finding, oldest first.

latest_verification.description: Most recent verification submission, where one exists.

finding_mutation_result.description: Payload of finding_claim and finding_update_status: the finding as it now stands.

previous_status.description: Status before the change, absent when nothing moved.

finding_submit_verification_result.description: Payload of finding_submit_verification. The finding is returned beside the verification so the agent can see the status the submission moved it to without a second call.

verification.description: The verification record, with status submitted.

finding.description: The finding as it now stands.

browser_take_screenshot_result.description: Payload of browser_take_screenshot. It carries a link and metadata and never image bytes, so the response is bounded whatever the page contains.

viewport.description: Viewport the capture was taken at.

full_page.description: Whether the whole document was captured.

url.description: URL the browser was on. Page-derived and untrusted.

tool_refusal.description: The error envelope of docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 5. It is deliberately not a frame: a refusal carries no type-selected data, and inventing an empty one would make an agent's success test depend on a field rather than on ok.

trust.description: Provenance of the refusal, which is the control plane.

instruction_policy.description: The policy that applies to any quoted content.

envelope.description: The common response envelope of docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 5, extended with the protocol version of section 14, the tool that answered and the instruction policy of docs/SECURITY.md section 11. Additive fields are permitted within a major version and a client ignores what it does not know (docs/API.md section 20). data is the payload selected by type.

protocol_version.description: MCP product protocol version. Stage 0 pins 1; any other value is refused rather than best-effort parsed.

ok.description: Whether the call succeeded. True in this shape; a refusal uses tool_refusal.

request_id.description: Identifier of the call, which joins a transcript line to its audit record.

type.description: Tool that answered, which selects the schema of data.

trust.description: Provenance of the content in data. Page-derived content is never returned without an untrusted label.

instruction_policy.description: The policy that applies to every string in data.

warnings.description: Degradations that did not stop the call succeeding.

data.description: Tool result. Its schema is selected by type, and each is bounded by its own x-max-bytes, which is the per-tool size limit of section 13.
